intro_en: In this lesson you learn to say who you gave something to. You also learn to say who you got something from, and who you learned from. The key point is how to use に and から. They work like the Tamil "-க்கு" (to) and "-இடம்" (from/with a person) endings. We also look at で for tools ("I eat with chopsticks"). You learn to ask "What is this in Japanese?". And you learn もう / まだ ("already / not yet"). The new words in this lesson are family words. There is one word for your own family members. There is a polite word for other people’s family members.

g07-1.explanation_en: In Lesson 6, で showed the place where an action happens. The same で can also show the tool, "with what / using what". 箸で食べます = "I eat with chopsticks". 日本語で書きます = "I write in Japanese". This is the Tamil "-ஆல் / -ஐக் கொண்டு" ending (by / using). バスで行きます (I go by bus) from Lesson 5 is this same で. For languages, Tamil uses "-இல்": "ஜப்பானிய மொழியில்" (in Japanese). But Japanese uses only で. Don’t use に.
g07-1.tamil_parallel_en: で for a tool matches the Tamil "-ஆல்" ending ("by / with"). "சாப்ஸ்டிக்ஸால்(-ஆல்) சாப்பிடுகிறேன்" ("I eat with chopsticks") = 箸で食べます. "தமிழில் எழுதுகிறேன்" ("I write in Tamil") = タミル語で書きます.
g07-1.pitfalls_en: 日本語に書きます ✗. For a language, use で, not に. Also, the same で shows a place (喫茶店で) and a tool (箸で). Don’t let that confuse you. The rest of the sentence makes it clear.

g07-2.explanation_en: Here is how to ask how to say a word in another language. 「ありがとう」はタミル語で何ですか = "What is “ありがとう” in Tamil?". Here 〜語で is the tool で you just saw. It means "using the Tamil language". The answer is "「நன்றி」です". The sentence order is the same as in Tamil: "‘தண்ணீர்’ ஜப்பானிய மொழியில் என்ன?" (What is “water” in Japanese?). The order is: the word, then は (the topic, what you are asking about), then the language + で, then 何, then ですか. Here 何 is read なん, because it comes before です. This sentence is very useful for asking your teacher in class.
g07-2.tamil_parallel_en: The question uses the same order as in Tamil. "‘நன்றி’ ஜப்பானிய மொழியில் என்ன?" ("What is “thank you” in Japanese?") = 「ナンドリ」は日本語で何ですか.
g07-2.formation_en: 「word」 + は + 〜語 + で + 何ですか  → 「word」です
g07-2.pitfalls_en: タミル語に何ですか ✗. For a language, use で. Here 何 is なん. Don’t read it as なに.

g07-3.explanation_en: Some verbs go to a person: give, lend, teach, write (to someone) and phone. With these, put に after the person. 妹に飴をあげます = "I give candy to my younger sister". This is the Tamil "-க்கு" ending (to). The word order is the same as Tamil: to whom に, then what を, then the verb. 兄は私に英語を教えます = "My older brother teaches me English". 電話をかけます (make a phone call) is in this group too: 母に電話をかけます. Note: use あげます when I give, or when someone gives to another person. When someone gives to me, Japanese uses a different word, くれます. You learn it in Lesson 24.
g07-3.tamil_parallel_en: に for the person who gets something is the Tamil "-க்கு" ending ("to"). The word order is the same. "தம்பிக்கு(-க்கு) புத்தகம் கொடுத்தேன்" ("I gave my younger brother a book") = 弟に本をあげました.
g07-3.formation_en: N(person) + に + N(thing) + を + あげます / 貸します / 教えます / 書きます / かけます
g07-3.pitfalls_en: 妹を飴をあげます ✗. The person who gets it takes に. The thing takes を. You can’t have two を. Think of the Tamil "-க்கு" in "தங்கைக்கு" (to my younger sister). Then you will get に right.

g07-4.explanation_en: Some verbs get something from a person: receive (もらいます), borrow (借ります) and learn (習います). With these, に or から shows who you get it from. 母に花瓶をもらいました = "I received a vase from my mother". This is the Tamil "-இடம் / -இடமிருந்து" (from a person). Be careful. With あげます above, に showed the person who gets it ("-க்கு", to). Here the same に shows the person who gives it ("-இடம்", from). The verb decides the direction. Tamil keeps "-க்கு" and "-இடம்" clearly apart. So look at the verb when you choose. から (from) works for a person. It also works for a group or a place (銀行から). に is only for a person.
g07-4.tamil_parallel_en: With "get" verbs, に / から match the Tamil "-இடம் / -இடமிருந்து" ("from"). "அம்மாவிடம்(-இடம்) பூ பெற்றேன்" ("I received flowers from my mother") = 母に花をもらいました. "நண்பரிடமிருந்து புத்தகம் கடன் வாங்கினேன்" ("I borrowed a book from a friend") = 友達から本を借りました.
g07-4.formation_en: N(person) + に / から + N(thing) + を + もらいます / 借ります / 習います
g07-4.pitfalls_en: With もらいます, に shows the giver. With あげます, に shows the person who gets it. 私は母にあげました (I gave it to my mother) ≠ 私は母にもらいました (I received it from my mother). If you are not sure, you can use から with もらいます.

g07-5.explanation_en: もう + past form = "I have already done it". もう食べました = "I have already eaten". As a question: もう食べましたか = "Have you eaten (yet)?". If yes, say はい、もう食べました. If no, say いいえ、まだです ("No, not yet"). This is just like the Tamil talk "சாப்பிட்டாச்சா? — ஆச்சு / இன்னும் இல்லை" (Have you eaten? Done / Not yet). Be careful. To say "I haven’t eaten yet", don’t say まだ食べませんでした. That means "I didn’t eat (at that time)", a statement about the past. At N5 level, just answer まだです. (The full form まだ食べていません comes after Lesson 14.)
g07-5.tamil_parallel_en: This is the everyday Tamil talk with "ஆச்சு / இன்னும் இல்லை". "ஏற்கனவே சாப்பிட்டாச்சு" ("I’ve already eaten") = もう食べました. "இன்னும் இல்லை" ("not yet") = まだです.
g07-5.formation_en: もう + V ました (か) ／ いいえ、まだです
g07-5.pitfalls_en: まだ食べませんでした ✗ (when you mean "I haven’t eaten yet"). Say まだです. The word もう can also mean "one more / more" (もう一つ). Here it only means "already".

g07-6.explanation_en: Japanese has two words for each family member. When you talk to others about your own family, use the humble word. Humble means you lower your own side to be polite. The humble words are: 父 father, 母 mother, 兄 older brother, 姉 older sister, 弟 younger brother, 妹 younger sister, 両親 parents. When you talk about someone else’s family, use the polite word. The polite words are: お父さん, お母さん, お兄さん, お姉さん, 弟さん, 妹さん, 奥さん. In Tamil, "என் அப்பா" (my father) and "உங்கள் அப்பா" (your father) use the same word. But Tamil also adds respect for other people’s family, as in "அப்பா அவர்கள்" or "உங்க அம்மாவுங்க". That helps you understand this. One exception: at home, when you call your own father and mother, you say お父さん and お母さん. It is like calling "அப்பா! அம்மா!" in Tamil. These polite words use the polite お〜 from Lesson 2 and 〜さん from Lesson 1.
g07-6.tamil_parallel_en: Tamil uses one word but adds respect for someone else’s family. Japanese changes the word. "என் அப்பா" ("my father") = 父. "உங்கள் அப்பா (அவர்கள்)" ("your (respected) father") = お父さん.
g07-6.formation_en: Your own family: 父・母・兄・姉・弟・妹・両親 ／ Someone else’s family: お父さん・お母さん・お兄さん・お姉さん・弟さん・妹さん・奥さん
g07-6.pitfalls_en: When you talk to others about your own father, 私のお父さんは医者です is wrong. Say 私の父. It also works the other way: 田中さんの父 ✗ → 田中さんのお父さん. Sound: people often mix up おとうさん (father) and おとうと (younger brother).

items.L07-q01: 両親 = りょうしん (பெற்றோர், parents). 両 is the long sound りょう. 親 is しん, not じん. Don’t mix it up with じん in 〜人.
items.L07-q02: 弟 = おとうと (தம்பி, younger brother). おとうさん is お父さん (அப்பா, father). They sound alike, so people often mix them up. There must be an う in the middle. And it is と, not ど.
items.L07-q03: 兄弟 = きょうだい (உடன்பிறந்தோர், siblings). きょう is a long sound. Here 弟 is だい, with the two dots. The short form きょだい is wrong.
items.L07-q04: はな = 花 (பூ, flower). 化 is only the bottom part of 花. It becomes 花 only with the grass part (艹) on top. 茶 (ちゃ) also has 艹, but it is a different word.
items.L07-q05: はは = 母 (என் அம்மா, my mother). 毎 (まい) and 海 (うみ) look like it, because they have a shape like 母. 父 (ちち) is father.
items.L07-q06: You learn a language from a teacher: 習います (கற்றுக்கொள்கிறேன், learn). 教えます turns it around: "I teach the teacher".
items.L07-q07: The first word on the phone is もしもし (ஹலோ, hello). はじめまして is for meeting someone face to face for the first time. さようなら is for saying goodbye.
items.L07-q08: You drink water from a glass = コップ (டம்ளர், glass/cup). お皿 (plate) and 箸 (chopsticks) are for eating, not drinking.
items.L07-q09: Japanese people eat with chopsticks = 箸 (சாப்ஸ்டிக்ஸ், chopsticks). コップ is for drinking. 花瓶 (vase) and 電話 (phone) are not for eating.
items.L07-q10: "No, not yet" = いいえ、まだです (இன்னும் இல்லை, not yet). もう (already) does not go with いいえ.
items.L07-q11: This is someone else’s (田中さんの) father. So use the polite word お父さん (அப்பா, father). 父 is only for your own father. 兄 and 母 are also humble words, so they don’t fit someone else’s family.
items.L07-q12: "My older brother teaches me" = "I learn from my older brother" (習います, கற்றுக்கொள்கிறேன், learn). If you keep 教えます and just swap the people, the meaning turns around.
items.L07-q13: "Tanaka received a watch from Yamada" = "Yamada gave Tanaka a watch" (山田さんは田中さんにあげました; கொடுத்தார், gave). もらう and あげる both use に, but they go in opposite directions. Note: when someone gives something to you, you can’t use あげました. You need くれました (Lesson 24).
items.L07-q14: "I borrowed it from a friend" = "My friend lent it to me" (貸しました, கடனாகக் கொடுத்தார், lent). 借りる (கடன் வாங்க, borrow) and 貸す (கடன் கொடுக்க, lend) sound alike, so people mix them up.
items.L07-q15: With あげます, the person who gets it takes に (like the Tamil "தங்கைக்கு", to my younger sister). を is only for the thing. One sentence can’t have two を.
items.L07-q16: With もらいます, the giver takes から (or に). で is for a tool or a place. が does not fit here.
items.L07-q17: Chopsticks are a tool ("சாப்ஸ்டிக்ஸால்", with chopsticks), so use で. With に it would mean "to the chopsticks".
items.L07-q18: Use で for a language (in English = using English). 英語に ✗.
items.L07-q19: もう (ஏற்கனவே, already) goes with the past ました. So the answer is 撮りましたか (எடுத்துவிட்டீர்களா?, have you taken it?). もう撮りますか makes no sense.
items.L07-q20: "Not yet" = まだです (இன்னும் இல்லை). A common mistake is まだ読みませんでした. That means "I didn’t read it (then)", not "I haven’t read it yet".
items.L07-q21: 電話をかけます means make a phone call. 電話 is the object (the thing), so use を. The person already has に (母に).
items.L07-q22: Order: to whom (友達に), then what (日本語の本を), then the verb (貸しました). The ★ slot is 本を. 日本語の tells you about 本, so it comes right before it.
items.L07-q23: Order: インドの母に (இந்தியாவில் உள்ள அம்மாவுக்கு, to my mother in India), then 電話を, then かけます. The ★ slot is 母に. インドの, with の, comes before it.
items.L07-q24: Order: time (誕生日に), then from whom (友達に), then what (花を), then the verb. The ★ slot is 花を. The verb is もらいました, so 友達に is the friend who gave it.
items.L07-q25: ［1］Chopsticks are a tool ("சாப்ஸ்டிக்ஸால்", with chopsticks), so use で. ［2］The person 教えます goes to ("எனக்கு", to me) takes に. から is only for "get" verbs. ［3］借りました needs the person you got it from ("அண்ணனிடமிருந்து", from my older brother). So use から. に is also correct, but it is not one of the choices.
